[text; page 1]

[text; page 1]
are affected by both the feed rate and the binder concentration. Droplet size and velocity
[text; page 1]
distributions, measured with a HiWatch system, showed that higher feed rates produce
[text; page 1]
larger droplets with faster velocities, therefore affecting the final morphology of the dried
[text; page 1]
product. The morphology of the dried granules was analyzed using inline SOPAT imaging.

While mercury intrusion porosimetry quantified the nano-pore volume and nano-pore size

[text; page 1]
morphology of the dried product. The findings show that, while raising the binder concen-

tration produces a more compact morphology with a lower nano-pore volume, higher feed
[text; page 1]
